title: Computational approach to evaluate scRNA-seq data quality and gene body coverage with SkewC
author: Abugessaisa, Hasegawa, et al.

steps.title: Organize gene body coverage files
steps.instruction: Place the output files generated by geneBodyCoverage.pl into a directory (default name ‘coverage’) that will be used as the input directory for SkewC.

steps.title: Define project and output parameters
steps.instruction: Choose a project name (default = ‘COV’; this name will appear on PDF outputs) and decide on an output directory for SkewC results (default = ‘skewc’).

steps.title: Run SkewC gene‑body coverage analysis
steps.instruction:
From the SkewC installation directory, execute the bash script 2_SkewC.sh with the required arguments: project name, input directory, output directory, and alpha value(s). The command template is:

~/SkewC$ bash 2_SkewC.sh $prjname $indir $outdir $alpha

where:
- $prjname = project name (default ‘COV’)
- $indir = directory containing geneBodyCoverage.pl files (default ‘coverage’)
- $outdir = directory for SkewC analysis files with index HTML (default ‘skewc’)
- $alpha = alpha for tclust computation (see below).

Timing: approximately 1–2 minutes for this step.

substeps.instruction:
Auto‑alpha mode (alpha not defined): the script selects the alpha value with the highest ctlcurves score.
Example: bash 2_SkewC.sh test input output

User‑specified single alpha (e.g., 0.1): the script runs tclust with the given alpha.
Example: bash 2_SkewC.sh test input output 0.1

User‑specified multiple alphas (e.g., 0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4): the script runs tclust for each listed alpha.
Example: bash 2_SkewC.sh test input output 0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4

description: We present a computational protocol that describes the technical details for the execution of SkewC, a quality assessment tool for scRNA-seq datasets. SkewC measures the quality of each single cell using gene body coverage and its skewness as quality metrics. The distribution of matched sequences throughout the whole gene (5′ to 3′ end) is used to determine the relative gene body coverage, a critical metric to assess the quality of scRNA-seq datasets.1 Using skewness of gene body coverage, SkewC defines two types of cells: typical cells (with prototypical gene body coverage) and skewed cells (with skewed gene body coverage). Because of the molecular characteristics of skewed cells and their impact on downstream analysis, SkewC recommends excluding cells with skewed gene body coverage from downstream analysis of scRNA-seq datasets.1 SkewC is implemented in the R and Perl computational languages. To enable operability, portability, and ease-of-use, the workflow is provided as a docker (and udocker) container and as a Singularity Image File (SIF) downloadable from SkewC GitHub repository here. SkewC can process any type of scRNA-seq datasets, (full length sequence, 5` -end and 3` -end target protocols). In our previous publications3,4 we demonstrated the implementation, integration, and utilization of SkewC in scRNA-seq data analysis.
